palette.notes: Desaturated drab greys, olive greens and browns for the booth and desk; one accent per entrant (red hat, blue face cast) carries identity. Clip 2 is fan art (red/black), ignored for the game's palette.

lighting: Flat, almost no light direction: faces get a single cool or green cast as a mood tint rather than lit shading; the booth is a dark frame around a lighter desk.
silhouette: Entrants are head-and-shoulders busts in a window: hat shape (cap, fur hat, peaked uniform cap) and glasses make each one readable at tiny size.

motion.timing: Not measured (no metrics file). Frames show near-static busts; change comes from cutting between entrants and UI elements (speech bubbles, documents) popping on, not from in-between animation.

texture: Chunky low-res pixels upscaled hard; scanline-like dark wood stripes behind the window; paper documents with tiny dithered text.
camera: Fixed split screen: top strip shows a small side-on queue at the checkpoint, bottom is the close-up booth and desk. Intro uses full-frame newspaper and propaganda cards.

acting.enters: Entrants walk up the queue as tiny figures in the top strip, then appear as a bust in the booth window.
acting.acts: Talk in short pixel-font speech bubbles stacked beside the window (one word per bubble); hand over papers that slide onto the desk.
acting.exits: Leave the window and walk off as a tiny figure in the top strip; the next one steps up.
acting.depth: Same characters shown twice at two scales: tiny in the background queue, large bust in the foreground booth.

techniques: two-scale staging: tiny walker in a background strip + large close-up bust
one accent colour per character on a drab base palette
stacked one-word speech bubbles timed as beats
fixed window frame so only the character changes
feel: drab grey-olive world + one accent colour per face + fixed booth window = tense, readable bureaucracy
for_fred: Give Fred a 'queue strip': show him tiny walking in a thin band at the top of the reel, then cut to him big in a window frame below; when he leaves the frame, let him reappear tiny in the strip doing something else. Keep the background drab so his orange reads.
